title: The Law of Christ
lead: Paul's phrase in Galatians 6:2, 'the law of Christ,' and its cousin 'under Christ's law' in 1 Corinthians 9:21. Readers have taken it as the Torah as Christ fulfills it, the command to love, the pattern of Christ's self-giving, a phrase Paul turned back on his opponents, or the law of Moses written on hearts by the Spirit.

sections.b: (1) The Torah as Christ interprets it (W. D. Davies). (2) The command to love (Galatians 5:14; Romans 13:10). (3) The pattern of Christ's self-giving (Hays). (4) An answer to the agitators' own slogan (Barclay). (5) The law of Moses fulfilled by the Spirit (Romans 8:4; Wright). The phrase is paired with the command to 'carry each other's heavy loads' in Galatians 6:2, which suggests the first sense is love in action.
sections.refs: Galatians 5:14; Galatians 6:2; Romans 8:4; Romans 13:8-10; 1 Corinthians 9:21; Matthew 5:17-20; James 1:25; James 2:8
